source_anchors.statement: Authors propose wavelength-dependent spin-wave loss in backward propagation.
Perspective identifies systematic sensitivity/tolerance and excitation-design studies.

units: a=hbar=J=1; gamma is amplitude decay rate; source and target have orthonormal FFT norm1
effort_convention: Fields named energy store dimensionless squared field norms/target weights, NOT calibrated microwave energy. No impedance, frequency Jacobian, or antenna-current calibration is claimed.
constraints: All drive spectra restricted to [0.1,2.8], norm1, spatial drive peak squared amplitude <=0.15
limitations: Effective spectral-drive surrogate, not a calibrated YIG/antenna/LLG simulation.
No strict finite spatial antenna support; a Gaussian antenna spectral transfer and hard spectral support are modeled.
High fidelity at target time does not imply whole-path shape preservation.
F measures complex-field shape; density-only overlap is reported separately.
Robust family is expected Tikhonov least-squares followed by unit normalization, not a proof of global robust optimum.

selection.rule: Among peak-feasible candidates satisfying F>=.95 (nominal or training5%quantile), maximise target energy; otherwise maximise F and flag infeasible.

target_position_statistics.note: Band projection and taper slightly alter the target from an unrestricted Gaussian.

interpretation.positive: At fixed input spectral norm, loss-aware regularisation improves complex-field fidelity while reducing absolute target weight.
negative_controls: Intensity-only shape overlap barely changes between blind and nominal aware designs.
Ensemble model does not outperform nominal family with the same training-based lambda selection.
Neither calibrated nor ensemble protocol reaches 95% heldout F>=.95 success in this run.
Peak cap .10 makes the F>=.95 target infeasible within the tested Tikhonov families, not necessarily among all possible inputs.
High fidelity at 4x loss has absolute target weight only about5e-7.
interpretation.review: Independent mathematical review found no conclusion-changing error after adding the same-selection-rule control.
